text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- At least a dozen weekend drownings at beaches.
- Palestinian Council Speaker Ahmed Korei watches Israeli flag burn.
- Yasser Arafat's wife Suha intervenes in Hebron monastery dispute.
- Rioting at Rachel's Tomb and in Hebron; more than 30 people hurt.
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon: Prime minister knows where to find me.
HAARETZ
- New Treasury programme: Big budget cut to take effect in September.
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai forbids meeting of Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli army commander in West Bank.
- 9,000 Russian experts and technicians in Iranian weapons industry.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu tending towards including Ariel Sharon in diplomatic-security team.
- Arab high-school pupil forced to learn eight hours weekly of Hebrew literature and language -- 2.5 times a Jewish pupil.
- Merrill-Lynch in negotiations to buy big package of shares in Bezeq Telecommunications from the state.
MAARIV
- Israel: Ahmed Korei's presence at burning of the Israeli flag destroys confidence. He tells Maariv: "Young people who burn flags today, I don't know what they'll burn tomorrow".
- Hebron gunman is released secretly from Israeli army -- and goes home.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Palestinian effort to widen disturbances to all of the West Bank.
